topics: p95 latency targets; concurrency (up to 200 concurrent sessions); streaming behavior for partial responses; token/sec benchmarking; cache/batching; VPC/on-prem constraints; SOC2/KMS; rollout plan
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-03 16:00 PT | Duration: 48m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Aria Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Nimbus CTO), Carlos Mendes (Nimbus Head of Platform), Jamal Ortiz (Nimbus ML Eng), Sophie Leung (Product)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — i'm Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off. Quick round robin?
[00:10] Priya Rao: Priya here, CTO at Nimbus, we build edge fleet orchestration and need low-latency inference for command-and-control prompts, mostly short queries but occasional long plan generation.
[00:22] Carlos Mendes: Carlos - platform, responsible for infra decisions; timeline is Q3 pilot.
[00:28] Jamal Ortiz: Jamal, ML infra, will own benchmarks and integration.
[00:33] Maya Chen: Great, main goal for today is to understand p95 targets, concurrency, streaming expectations and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private fits. Liam, Aria — you on the line for technical details?
[00:42] Liam O'Connor: Yep, hi all. I'll run through throughput & latency questions then we can map to Redwood options.
[00:48] [00:50] Jamal Ortiz: Quick note — our real-time loop wants p95 <= 120ms for short completion (<= 60 tokens) and we can accept 800-1200ms for long planning (400-800 tokens). Concurrency needs to hit bursts to 150-200 simultaneous sessions.
[01:10] Maya Chen: Nice, that's super helpful. Do you see a consistent proportion of short vs long?
[01:18] Jamal Ortiz: About 70% short, 25% medium (100-300 tokens), 5% long. We also use streaming to get partial outputs to the robot while generation continues.
[01:28] Liam O'Connor: Ok so streaming is critical — that shifts cost/latency tradeoffs. A few clarifying q's: what model family are you planning to use? Open weights or commercial endpoints?
[01:40] Priya Rao: We're open to using open models quantized for on-prem, but for the pilot we'd like to test hosted first to iterate quickly. Concern is P95 for hosted — does Redwood expose infra SLAs for p95?
[01:52] Maya Chen: Hosted has published performance profiles per model; we provide observed p95 under typical load. Dedicated gives you predictable capacity guarantees; Private gives you full control but higher ops. We can commit to throughput SLAs on Dedicated contracts.
[02:07] [02:10] Carlos Mendes: Important — network path variability. If we use Hosted, streaming from Redwood to our edge gateways must be reliable; do you support persistent SSE/TCP streaming and reconnect semantics?
[02:22] Aria Patel: Yes, we have streaming via chunked transfer / SSE and resumable streams on our SDK. For high churn we recommend edge proxies or using Dedicated in the same cloud region to reduce jitter.
[02:36] Liam O'Connor: For benchmarking we'll want to reproduce your runtime: model, sequence lengths, beam/temperature settings, tokens per second. We'll also measure token/sec throughput at concurrency levels: 1, 10, 50, 100, 200.
[02:51] Jamal Ortiz: That sounds good. On the p95 target for short completions — 120ms is aggressive. Curious, is that end-to-end or just model decode?
[03:00] Maya Chen: Good call — clarify end-to-end vs model-only.
[03:03] Jamal Ortiz: End-to-end, from request arrival at our gateway to first token displayed on the robot UI.
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: Ok that includes network + our runtime. For short responses decoding may be sub-100ms on optimized kernels with small batch sizes but network and SDK latency matter. On Dedicated with colocated infra hitting 120ms p95 is achievable for some smaller models; for larger models you'd need quantized variants and lower sequence lengths.
[03:29] [03:30] Priya Rao: What about batching and KV-cache warmup? Our workload has repeated contexts across same robot sessions, can cache help?
[03:40] Aria Patel: Absolutely. KV/prefix caching is one of our levers — if you have repeated history per session we can cache the KV layers to reduce per-token decode cost. Caching plus small batching gets you much lower tail latency.
[03:53] Jamal Ortiz: Does caching interact badly with streaming? We need partial tokens ASAP.
[03:58] Liam O'Connor: It shouldn't — caching speeds up decode; streaming is an output mechanism. The key is how the runtime flushes tokens; we can configure smaller decode chunks to surface tokens earlier at slight throughput impact.
[04:12] [04:15] Carlos Mendes: Let's talk numbers: can you run 200-concurrency test for 50-token prompts and report p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec, and then a long 500-token test with streaming?
[04:28] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll propose a benchmark plan. We'll need sample prompts and traces. Liam can provision an endpoint with identical model variant we'll test on.
[04:36] Liam O'Connor: We'll also provide the harness (k6 + custom runner) and the metrics layout (latency histograms, token throughput, cpu/gpu utilization). Note: token/sec reported can be noisy; we prefer reporting decoded tokens/sec and effective tokens/sec including network time.
[04:55] [05:00] Priya Rao: Security question — if we go Hosted for the pilot, how is customer data handled? Do you offer separate tenancy or guaranteed deletion?
[05:10] Maya Chen: Hosted keeps isolation per account; we log request metadata for debugging but payload retention is configurable. We support customer-managed KMS for key material in Dedicated and Private. We'll share SOC 2 & ISO artifacts.
[05:24] Jamal Ortiz: For Dedicated, what does capacity provisioning look like? We want headroom for 2x peak.
[05:30] Aria Patel: Dedicated is provisioned as GPU pools; you can set a reserved base and burst pools. We size to meet p95 SLOs — recommended reserve for 2x peak if you require hard SLOs.
[05:42] [05:45] Sophie Leung: Pricing — how does streaming impact cost vs non-streaming?
[05:50] Maya Chen: Streaming doesn't change per-token compute but may add small network egress costs for chunked results. Our pricing is token-based for Hosted; Dedicated is capacity pricing + usage delta. We'll include streaming examples in the pricing doc.
[06:05] Carlos Mendes: Any particular hardware you'd recommend for Private/on-prem to hit these p95s for 120ms on short tokens?
[06:12] Liam O'Connor: For sub-150ms on short decodes we recommend A100 80GB or RTX 6000 class with optimized kernels and int8 quantization. Lower memory GPUs are possible with model sharding but add latency.
[06:25] [06:30] Jamal Ortiz: Can Redwood's runtime do continuous batching while preserving per-request latency goals? Our concern is batching = higher p95.
[06:38] Aria Patel: Our runtime supports dynamic batching with per-route latency caps; if a request is latency-sensitive we can run it in a low-latency lane (smaller batch) while background lanes batch for throughput. That's part of Optimize recommendations.
[06:51] Maya Chen: Quick interjection — a few known gotchas: 1) Cold KV cache can spike p95 initially, 2) Network egress spikes if you surface every token, 3) Model quantization changes accuracy. We can simulate all these in the benchmark.
[07:06] [07:10] Priya Rao: Ok — about accuracy, Jamal's worried that quantization may break some instruction following. Can we test quality/regression as part of the pilot?
[07:19] Liam O'Connor: Yes we usually run an eval set of prompts and compare outputs across model variants, quantization levels, and ensure top-line metrics like task success or F1 stay within threshold. We'll include that in the bench.
[07:30] [07:35] Carlos Mendes: Networking again — do you support private link/VPC peering? We have strict firewall and NACL rules.
[07:42] Aria Patel: Yep — Dedicated supports VPC peering and Private deployment gives you full VPC control on customer side. For Hosted we offer private link in select regions.
[07:53] Jamal Ortiz: For the benchmark, please include a breakdown: request queuing time, app->edge network, edge->runtime, decode time, token flush time, plus GPU util.
[08:05] Liam O'Connor: We'll include all those traces and provide sample dashboards. Also if you can provide a few production traces we can more accurately simulate arrival patterns (bursty vs steady).
[08:16] [08:20] Sophie Leung: What's a realistic timeline for the run and getting results?
[08:24] Maya Chen: If we get the prompts/traces by Friday (2025-06-06), we can provision and run initial tests the week of 6/9 and deliver a results deck by 6/13.
[08:34] Priya Rao: Sounds good. Another minor point — we use mTLS from our gateways. Does Redwood accept client certs for authentication on Dedicated or Private?
[08:45] Aria Patel: Private supports mTLS and mutual auth; Dedicated can be configured with customer-managed certs. Hosted uses token-based auth by default.
[08:55] [09:00] Carlos Mendes: For the p95 target, what if the numbers miss? Do you provide auto-fallback to a lighter model to keep latency bounded?
[09:08] Liam O'Connor: Yes — smart routing can auto-fallback to a smaller model variant or degrade to non-streaming/shorter sequence if SLOs are breached. You can configure fallback policies per route.
[09:20] Jamal Ortiz: Very useful. Ok let's capture next steps.
[09:25] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to run token/sec + latency benchmarks at 1/10/50/100/200 concurrency for 50-token and 500-token workloads, include p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, utilization. Nimbus to provide prompts, traces, and success criteria. We'll share security pack and initial pricing.
[09:40] Priya Rao: And we'll review results and decide between Hosted pilot or Dedicated reserve.
[09:45] Maya Chen: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the deeper technical run-through.
[09:50] [09:52] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: Automated transcription confused a few model names (e.g., reported 'Redwood Dedicate' instead of Dedicated). Some interruptions overlapped, may see "uh" and repeated words.

References/Links mentioned: "benchmark harness (k6 + custom runner) - link to be shared", "security packet - SOC2/ISO docs - link to be shared", "pricing sheet - link to be shared"
notes: Call included AE+SE from Redwood. Customer emphasis on stringent p95 for short completions and streaming. Agreed to run benchmarks and share security docs. Transcription contains minor ASR errors (product names).
meeting_outcome: Agreement to run benchmark; follow-up deep dive scheduled pending prompt set; potential Dedicated pilot if numbers meet SLOs.
